content:
The image shows a cross-section of a corn ear viewed from the tip/butt end. Key observations:

- **White cottony/fluffy mold** growing from the center (cob area) outward between and around kernels
- **Kernels appear discolored** — grayish, tan, with some pink/red streaking visible between kernels
- **Mold appears white to off-white**, not pink-red, not green, not olive
- The mold is growing from the **base/center outward**, covering the cob face
- Some kernels show tan/brown discoloration with possible pinkish hues

Now matching to candidates:

- **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: White mold starting at the **base** of the ear — this cross-section shows white mold emanating from the center/base of the cut end, which is consistent. Bleached husks visible in background. No pinkish coloration.
- **Fusarium**: White to pink/salmon cottony mold on **scattered kernels**, starburst pattern — the mold here is more uniform and central, not scattered.
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Pinkish-white to pink-red mold at the **tip** — the color here lacks the strong pink/red of Gibberella.

The white mold growing from the center (base) of the ear with grayish discolored kernels and visible white fluffy mycelium strongly matches **Ear_rots_Diplodia**. The husks in the background also appear bleached/light-colored consistent with the description.

{"prediction": "Ear_rots_Diplodia", "confidence": 0.72, "reasoning": "White cottony mycelium growing from the central cob area outward across the kernel face, with grayish-tan discolored kernels and bleached husks visible in the background. The white (not pink, not green) mold originating from the base/center matches Diplodia ear rot's characteristic white basal mold. Fusarium would show scattered pink/salmon mold with starburst patterns; Gibberella would show stronger pinkish-red coloration at the tip."}
